text:
Trevor Zegras's week was about ten minutes on the bench. He took a 10-minute misconduct in a loss for tapping his stick at a referee, per Sportskeeda, and The New York Times and Broad Street Hockey both reported that Rick Tocchet was not happy about it. For a player who came to Philadelphia from Anaheim in 2025 needing a fresh start, that is the kind of headline that sticks.

On the ice the picture is mixed. He has 14 points in 18 games and eight on the power play, but only four goals on 5.71 expected, shooting 10.5 percent. The worrying number is at five on five: the Flyers get 36.2 percent of the expected goals with him out there, eight points worse than without him.

That is a strange fit with last season, when Evolving-Hockey rated him 47th among 401 forwards at 2.1 wins above replacement, driving offense in the 94th percentile against tough competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said 55 percent of his shots came off the rush. When he is good, he is fast and loose. Watch whether the misconduct changes his minutes; he is playing 18:46 a night now.
headline: Zegras, a misconduct, and a coach's patience
